current_answer: NLnet CodeSupply is open to 3 November 2026, 12:00 CET for open-source software supply-chain R&D. A first application can request EUR 5,000–50,000, but selection is competitive and a strong European dimension is required. The live form needs a technical case and costed work plan; generative-AI assistance must be disclosed with a prompt log. Review is estimated at three to five months after the deadline and selected work is paid after milestones, not up front.

catalogue_card.question: Can you prepare a CodeSupply proposal before 3 November?
catalogue_card.text: The call is open to individuals and organisations working on open-source software supply-chain R&D. Request EUR 5,000–50,000, but first check the European rule, costed tasks and AI-use log. NLnet reviews after the deadline and pays selected work after milestones—not up front.

summary: The first-call deadline is 3 November 2026, 12:00 CET; the shared form is live and attachments are optional.
The form asks for a concise technical case, task/rate budget, comparison with existing work, technical risks, ecosystem, experience and other funding.
Disclose generative-AI help with a prompt log; approval and the applicant-specific award remain unknown.

Applicant-specific European fit, award, review outcome and first payment date are unknown.
